title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
title_zh: Dream-RSI: 递归自我改进通过演化世界实现

paragraphs.en: Recursive self-improvement is becoming essential for autonomous AI agents, whose progress depends on discovering high-value solutions across complex domains. Effective exploration drives this process, yet managing and improving exploration strategies remains a major bottleneck. Current systems face a fundamental dilemma: fixed strategies fail to adapt as search spaces scale, while online policy optimization must navigate vast meta-search spaces under delayed, expensive feedback from long-horizon rollouts. We introduce Dream-RSI , a framework for scalable, recursively self-improving exploration. A lightweight orchestration layer makes exploration explicit and programmable while leaving the underlying base agent unchanged. Our key insight is that accumulated discovery history can act as a replay simulator over the realized search space. By dreaming within this simulator built from historical discovery trees, Dream-RSI obtains immediate, low-cost off-policy feedback to evaluate and refine exploration policies without repeated, expensive online evaluation. The improved policy is then redeployed online to drive further discovery, continuously expanding the simulator pool in a self-improving loop. Across 9 tasks in 4 domains, Dream-RSI achieves competitive quality and improves discovery efficiency in several settings. github.com/zhengkid/Dream-RSI | dream-rsi.com

paragraphs.en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has emerged as an ambitious goal for autonomous AI systems ( Liu et al., 2026c ) . A common mechanism underlying RSI is an iterative loop wherein agents propose candidate solutions, evaluate outcomes, and fold the resulting feedback into subsequent iterations. Such loops have driven substantial progress across algorithm design ( Novikov et al., 2025 ; Romera-Paredes et al., 2024 ) , open-ended mathematical optimization ( Georgiev et al., 2025 ; Anthropic, 2026 ) , systems design ( Jaber and Jaber, 2026 ; Cao et al., 2026 ) , and agent self-improvement ( Zhang et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026c ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2026a ) . As agents grow stronger and self-improvement targets grow harder, discovery demands long-horizon exploration over vast search spaces, often spanning thousands of proposal-evaluation cycles ( Ye et al., 2026 ; OpenAI, 2026 ) . At this scale, orchestrating exploration becomes critical ( Zheng et al., 2026b ) : poor exploration wastes computation and time, sharply limiting the efficiency and scalability of RSI.
paragraphs.zh: 递归自我改进（RSI）已成为自主人工智能系统的一个雄心勃勃的目标（Liu et al., 2026c）。 RSI 的一个常见机制是迭代循环，其中智能体提出候选解决方案、评估结果，并将由此产生的反馈融入后续迭代。 此类循环已在算法设计（Novikov et al., 2025；Romera-Paredes et al., 2024）、开放式数学优化（Georgiev et al., 2025；Anthropic, 2026）、系统设计（Jaber and Jaber, 2026；Cao et al., 2026）以及智能体自我改进（Zhang et al., 2026b；Zhang et al., 2026c；Lee et al., 2026；Zheng et al., 2026a）方面推动了重大进展。 随着智能体变得更强、自我改进的目标变得更难，发现过程需要在广阔的搜索空间中进行长程探索，往往涉及数千次提案-评估循环（Ye et al., 2026；OpenAI, 2026）。 在这样的规模下，探索的编排变得至关重要（Zheng et al., 2026b）：糟糕的探索会浪费计算资源和时间，严重限制 RSI 的效率和可扩展性。

paragraphs.en: Existing approaches largely rely on manually designed exploration strategies that stay fixed throughout discovery ( Novikov et al., 2025 ; Yan et al., 2026b ; Du et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ; Ye et al., 2026 ) . Such strategies cannot learn from accumulated experience and may repeatedly spend computation on unproductive search directions. Recent work therefore attempts to optimize exploration policies online ( Liu et al., 2026a ) , but this faces two fundamental bottlenecks. First, meta-level feedback is delayed and expensive. Unlike evaluating a single candidate, assessing an exploration policy requires observing how it shapes discovery over many proposal–evaluation cycles. Second, the meta-policy space is vast, so many alternatives must be tried before a good one is found. Together, these make meta-level improvement costly. Each policy demands a long online rollout before yielding useful signal, making the self-improvement loop hard to close at the exploration layer.
paragraphs.zh: 现有方法主要依赖人工设计且在发现过程中保持固定的探索策略（Novikov et al., 2025；Yan et al., 2026b；Du et al., 2026；Jiang et al., 2026；Ye et al., 2026）。 这类策略无法从积累的经验中学习，并可能反复将计算花费在无效的搜索方向上。 因此，近期工作尝试在线优化探索策略（Liu et al., 2026a），但这面临两个根本性瓶颈。 首先，元层反馈是延迟且昂贵的。 与评估单个候选方案不同，评估一个探索策略需要观察它在多次提案—评估循环中如何塑造发现过程。 其次，元策略空间非常庞大，因此在找到一个好的策略之前必须尝试许多替代方案。 这两者叠加，使元层的改进成本高昂。 每个策略都需要经过漫长的在线推演才能产生有用的信号，使得自我改进闭环难以在探索层完成。

paragraphs.en: To address these bottlenecks, we want to design a fast and cheap simulator of discovery to prune exploration policies before costly online deployment. Surprisingly, completed discovery histories already provide such a simulator. Prior work treats past history merely as static textual context ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Ouyang et al., 2026b ) or as training data for fine-tuning ( Yuksekgonul et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) . Yet a completed discovery process inherently records a structured tree of exploration decisions and their realized code-execution outcomes. By analogy to model-based reinforcement learning and World Models ( Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018 ; Hafner et al., 2023 ) (§ 2 ), this discovery history can serve as a replay simulator 1 1 1 We use replay simulator and world interchangeably. . Figure 2 shows an alternative strategy can navigate this pre-recorded tree, traversing different subsets of branches in different orders, with different parallel groupings and stopping decisions. Since all execution results are locally stored, evaluating a new strategy requires only reading past records. This turns meta-policy improvement from expensive online trial-and-error into a fast, simulation-based “dreaming” procedure.

paragraphs.en: Building on this insight, we introduce Dream-RSI , a framework for scalable, recursively self-improving meta-exploration in agent-driven discovery. We first make exploration programmable through a lightweight orchestration layer that controls branching, parallelism, and stopping while leaving the underlying base agent unchanged. To improve this policy, Dream-RSI follows a self-improvement loop (Figure 1 ): (1) Online Exploration , where the current policy drives real-world discovery and logs execution traces; (2) Replay Simulator Construction , where recorded discovery trees become a reusable replay simulator pool; and (3) Dreaming-based Policy Improvement , where candidate policies are cheaply evaluated by dreaming over the simulator. The updated policy is redeployed online, generating new experience that expands the simulator pool and closing an RSI loop at the meta-exploration layer. We evaluate Dream-RSI on 9 discovery tasks across four domains. On algorithm engineering (Lasso path solver), it outperforms sklearn and strong baselines while using up to 162 × 162\times fewer agent calls than SimpleTES . On mathematical optimization, it matches or exceeds the best results among the compared baselines on two of three tasks. On GPU kernel engineering (KernelBench), it reaches similar speeds with 1.79 × 1.79\times – 2.43 × 2.43\times fewer generations, or improves kernel performance by up to 2.09 × 2.09\times under a comparable budget. On harness optimization , it improves the seed harness by over 8 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
paragraphs.zh: 基于这一洞见，我们提出 Dream-RSI，一个用于智能体驱动发现中可扩展、递归自我改进元探索的框架。 我们首先通过一个轻量级的编排层使探索变得可编程，该层控制分支、并行与停止，同时保持底层基础智能体不变。 为了改进这一策略，Dream-RSI 遵循一个自我改进循环（图 1）：(1) 在线探索，当前策略驱动真实世界的发现并记录执行轨迹；(2) 回放模拟器构建，将记录的发现树转化为可复用的回放模拟器池；(3) 基于做梦的策略改进，通过在模拟器上做梦以低成本评估候选策略。 更新后的策略被重新部署到线上，生成扩展模拟器池的新经验，从而在元探索层闭合一个递归自我改进（RSI）循环。 我们在四个领域的 9 个发现任务上评估 Dream-RSI。 在算法工程（Lasso 路径求解器）上，它优于 sklearn 和强基线，同时使用的智能体调用次数最多比 SimpleTES 少 162 × 162\times 倍。 在数学优化上，它在三个任务中的两个上达到或超过所比较基线中的最佳结果。 在 GPU 内核工程（KernelBench）上，它以少 1.79 × 1.79\times–2.43 × 2.43\times 倍的生成次数达到相近的速度，或在相近预算下将内核性能提升最多 2.09 × 2.09\times 倍。 在测试框架（harness）优化上，它在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上将种子测试框架提升超过 8 分。

paragraphs.en: Our contributions are: 1) History as Replay Simulator. paragraphs.en: Consider an agent navigating an unfamiliar environment. On its first attempt it wanders, hits dead ends, and backtracks — but in doing so it builds a map. That map is reusable: a new policy can plan over it, skip known dead ends, revisit earlier choices, and compare routes without physically walking them again ( Gupta et al., 2017 ) . This is the logic of model-based reinforcement learning ( Sutton, 1990 ; M. Moerland et al., 2023 ) . A model of how the environment responds to actions lets policies be trained or evaluated in simulation instead of through repeated real interaction ( Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018 ) . The Dreamer family ( Hafner et al., 2019 ; Hafner et al., 2020 ; Hafner et al., 2023 ; Hafner et al., 2025 ) is the clearest example: learn a compact dynamics model from collected experience, then improve the policy by imagining trajectories inside it.

paragraphs.en: Long-horizon discovery has the same structure. An exploration policy decides which directions to pursue, which candidates to refine, what to branch on in parallel, and when to stop. Running it online leaves behind a structured history — branches explored, decisions made, costs incurred, outcomes observed. As shown in Figure 2 , we treat this history as an empirical replay simulator: a grounded model of the part of the discovery space already seen. Inside this simulator, a different exploration policy simply traces a different path through the recorded discovery tree, choosing other branches, another ordering, a different degree of parallelism, or an earlier stopping point. Scoring that path only requires revealing outcomes already stored along it; no rerun of the coding agent or evaluator is needed. One expensive online run therefore funds many cheap evaluations of alternative strategies.
paragraphs.zh: 长周期探索具有相同的结构。 一个探索策略决定 pursue 哪些方向、refine 哪些候选、并行 branch 哪些节点，以及何时停止。 在线运行它会留下一个结构化的历史——已探索的分支、已做出的决策、已付出的成本、已观察到的结果。 如图 2 所示，我们将这一历史视为一个经验回放模拟器：一个针对探索空间中已被见过部分的有据可依的模型。 在这个模拟器内部，另一个探索策略只需在已记录的探索树中沿一条不同的路径行进，选择其他分支、另一种顺序、不同的并行程度，或更早的停止点。 对该路径打分只需揭示其中已存储的结果；无需重新运行编码智能体或评估器。 因此，一次昂贵的在线运行可以支撑对多种替代策略的大量廉价评估。

paragraphs.en: As shown in Figure 1 , Dream-RSI alternates between online exploration and offline “dreaming” for policy evaluation to improve the exploration policy that allocates discovery computation. For online rollout, the exploration policy directs a fixed discovery agent to generate a tree-structure discovery trace, where each node in the tree is an discovery attempt and is scored by a fixed evaluator . The discovery tree then becomes a replay world : alternative policies can be re-evaluated against stored outcomes. In the offline dreaming phase, a fixed agent iteratively revises the code for the exploration policy, and every revision is evaluated in all stored replay worlds. The best version is then deployed for the next online rollout. Only the policy code changes; the models, evaluator, and execution interfaces stay fixed.

The history informs exploration but is kept separate from the tree under construction. Let 𝒯 t k \mathcal{T}_{t}^{k} be the discovery tree after k k completed rounds at iteration t t , with 𝒯 t 0 = { r } \mathcal{T}_{t}^{0}=\{r\} , and allow at most K 1 K_{1} rounds. At round k < K 1 k<K_{1} , the policy picks C t k ∈ A ⁡ ( 𝒯 t k , W ) C_{t}^{k}\in A(\mathcal{T}_{t}^{k};W) and assigns each v ∈ C t k v\in C_{t}^{k} to a worker, which resumes v v ’s workspace, generates a candidate, and evaluates it. These attempts run in parallel and each adds one child to its selected parent. Thus, every v ∈ C t k v\in C_{t}^{k} is attached with a child, giving 𝒯 t k + 1 \mathcal{T}_{t}^{k+1} . paragraphs.en: We evaluate Dream-RSI on algorithm engineering, kernel optimization, mathematical optimization, and harness optimization. We primarily use Gemini-3.1-Pro for scientific discovery experiments, with additional Lasso experiments using Gemini-3.7-Flash to assess applicability across backbones. For harness optimization, we use Claude Opus 4.8 with Claude Code. On the scientific discovery tasks, our main controlled baseline is Recursive Fixed Exploration. Both methods use identical discovery agents, evaluators, initialization, per-round budget limits, and the same hand-designed starting policy. From the second round onward, Recursive Fixed Exploration keeps its policy fixed, while Dream-RSI updates it through replay-based dreaming over accumulated discovery history. For harness optimization, we focus on end-to-end performance and omit the fixed-policy comparison due to its substantial cost: an additional full search is estimated to cost over $100,000. We measure discovery cost as the cumulative number of discovery-agent calls.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在算法工程、内核优化、数学优化和测试框架优化上评估 Dream-RSI。 我们主要使用 Gemini-3.1-Pro 进行科学发现实验，并额外使用 Gemini-3.7-Flash 进行 Lasso 实验，以评估其在不同骨干模型上的适用性。 在测试框架优化方面，我们使用 Claude Opus 4.8 配合 Claude Code。 在科学发现任务上，我们的主要受控基线是递归固定探索（Recursive Fixed Exploration）。 两种方法使用完全相同的发现智能体、评估器、初始化、每轮预算限制，以及相同的人工设计的起始策略。 从第二轮开始，递归固定探索保持其策略固定，而 Dream-RSI 则通过基于回放的做梦（dreaming）在累积的发现历史上更新策略。 对于测试框架优化，我们关注端到端性能，并因成本过高而省略固定策略对比：额外一次完整搜索预计花费超过 10 万美元。 我们将发现成本衡量为发现智能体调用次数的累计值。

paragraphs.en: The goal of kernel engineering is to discover high-performance kernel implementations while preserving numerical correctness. We use four representative KernelBench tasks ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ) : VGG16 , LayerNorm , ConvDiv , and ConvMax . Candidates are scored by execution performance, measured as inverse runtime ( 1 / ms 1/\mathrm{ms} ), subject to correctness checks against the reference implementation. With Gemini-3.1 Pro as the coding agent, we compare Dream-RSI against Recursive Fixed Exploration under an identical evaluation protocol and initialization, and against the strong PaceEvolve baseline ( Yan et al., 2026b ) , whose maximum discovery time we cap at two days for fairness.
paragraphs.zh: 核工程的目标是在保持数值正确性的前提下发现高性能的核实现。 我们使用四个代表性的 KernelBench 任务（Ouyang 等，2025）：VGG16、LayerNorm、ConvDiv 和 ConvMax。 候选方案按执行性能打分，性能以运行时间的倒数（1/ms）衡量，同时须通过与参考实现的正确性检验。 以 Gemini-3.1 Pro 作为编码智能体，我们在相同的评估协议和初始化条件下，将 Dream-RSI 与递归固定探索进行比较，并与强大的 PaceEvolve 基线（Yan 等，2026b）进行比较，为公平起见，我们将其最长发现时间限制为两天。

paragraphs.en: Figure 3 shows discovery trajectories as the number of generations increases. On VGG16 and LayerNorm, Dream-RSI matches final performance with 2.43 × 2.43\times and 1.79 × 1.79\times fewer generations. On ConvDiv and ConvMax, under comparable budgets, it achieves 2.09 × 2.09\times and 1.44 × 1.44\times higher performance. Adapting the exploration policy across recursive rounds thus improves both the efficiency and the effectiveness of long-horizon discovery, and Dream-RSI surpasses PACEvolve in kernel performance (Detailed PACEvolve scaling curves are provided in Appendix C .). Appendix E.2 gives the discovered ConvDiv kernel. Rather than optimizing convolution in isolation, it restructures the operator chain around downstream pooling and reduction. Adjacent convolution outputs are max-pooled immediately, while width pooling and subsequent reductions run directly on register-resident values, avoiding materialization of convolution and pooled feature maps. Linear operations, such as scaling, averaging, and bias accumulation, are deferred to a lightweight final reduction.

paragraphs.en: In this task, we consider Lasso Regularization Path as our algorithm-engineering task, a fundamental computational primitive in high-dimensional statistics that is widely used in model selection and cross-validation across domains such as genomics and finance. We follow the benchmark setting of SimpleTES ( Ye et al., 2026 ) , where the goal is to discover efficient implementations of the complete Lasso regularization path while preserving numerical correctness. During discovery, we use the same 17 synthetic instances as SimpleTES, which cover diverse problem regimes in terms of dimensionality, sparsity, feature correlation, and active-set structure. To evaluate whether the discovered algorithms generalize beyond the search distribution, we additionally evaluate them on six held-out downstream datasets spanning biological and non-biological domains. We compare against standard Lasso solvers sklearn ( Pedregosa et al., 2011 ) and glmnet ( Friedman et al., 2010 ) , as well as SimpleTES ( Ye et al., 2026 ) . We run both controlled baseline and Dream-RSI for 5 rounds.
paragraphs.zh: 在本任务中，我们将 Lasso 正则化路径作为我们的算法工程任务，它是高维统计中的一个基础计算原语，被广泛用于基因组学和金融等领域的模型选择与交叉验证。 我们遵循 SimpleTES（Ye et al., 2026）的基准设置，其目标是在保持数值正确性的前提下，发现完整 Lasso 正则化路径的高效实现。 在发现过程中，我们使用与 SimpleTES 相同的 17 个合成实例，这些实例在维度、稀疏性、特征相关性和活动集结构方面覆盖了多样的问题情形。 为了评估所发现的算法能否泛化到搜索分布之外，我们还在六个留出的下游数据集上对它们进行了额外评估，这些数据集涵盖生物与非生物领域。 我们与标准 Lasso 求解器 sklearn（Pedregosa et al., 2011）和 glmnet（Friedman et al., 2010），以及 SimpleTES（Ye et al., 2026）进行比较。 我们将受控基线与 Dream-RSI 各运行 5 轮。

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 (a) summarizes the Lasso discovery results. Across both discovery-agent backbones, Dream-RSI achieves a better downstream quality–compute trade-off than Recursive Fixed Exploration. With Gemini-3.1 Pro, it reduces the average runtime across the six held-out datasets from 3587.1 ms to 2931.0 ms while using only 317 discovery-agent calls, compared with 550 calls for fixed exploration. With Gemini-3.7-Flash, Dream-RSI further reduces the average runtime from 2516.7 ms to 2350.6 ms using 1879 calls instead of 3200. Despite using substantially less discovery compute, the resulting solvers also outperform the standard sklearn and glmnet implementations on all six held-out datasets. Relative to SimpleTES’s reported 51,200 generations, our Pro and Flash runs use approximately 162 × \times and 27 × \times fewer discovery-agent calls, respectively, with lower average downstream runtime, although these comparisons use different model backbones. For 3.1 Pro, the average improvement over fixed exploration is driven by RCV1, despite slower runtimes on the other five datasets. For 3.7 Flash, runtime improves on five of the six datasets.

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 (b) shows the trajectory of downstream performance across recursive discovery rounds against cumulative discovery compute. By design, both methods behave identically in the first round. Afterward, Recursive Fixed Exploration keeps a static exploration policy, while Dream-RSI iteratively refines and redeploys its policy by dreaming over accumulated discovery history. By the final round, Dream-RSI achieves lower average downstream runtime with fewer discovery-agent calls than Recursive Fixed Exploration on both backbones. We further examine the discovered solver, whose implementation appears in Appendix E.1 . Unlike SimpleTES , which switches between LARS and coordinate descent by problem dimension, the discovered solver makes the active-set optimization itself adaptive. It pairs strong-rule screening with Cauchy–Schwarz KKT pruning, computing exact gradients only when necessary and falling back to a full refresh once pruning loses effectiveness.

paragraphs.en: We further investigate how the nature of the historical inductive bias affects long-horizon discovery. A natural alternative for utilizing history is to abstract prior trajectories into high-level directional insights, which are directly injected into the prompt as explicit semantic guidance for subsequent rounds. To evaluate the efficacy of this prompt-level semantic guidance, we apply it to both Recursive Fixed Exploration and Dream-RSI . As illustrated in Figure 6 , explicit directional guidance yields lower final performance for both methods on ConvDiv. This suggests that such guidance may constrain exploration.

paragraphs.en: Figure 7 illustrates how the learned exploration policy evolves across recursive rounds on ConvDiv. paragraphs.en: LLM-based discovery systems iteratively generate, evaluate, and refine candidate solutions using prior artifacts and feedback, as in AlphaEvolve ( Novikov et al., 2025 ) , OpenEvolve ( Sharma, 2025 ) , CodeEvolve ( Assumpção et al., 2025 ) , ShinkaEvolve ( Lange et al., 2026 ) , PACEvolve ( Yan et al., 2026b ) , DeltaEvolve ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) and MLEvolve Du et al. (2026) . More recent work emphasizes the importance of exploration itself: SkyDiscover provides adaptive discovery infrastructure ( Liu et al., 2026b ) , SwarmResearch dynamically orchestrates multiple search branches ( Virk et al., 2026 ) , and EvoX ( Liu et al., 2026a ) explicitly optimizes search strategies rather than only candidate solutions. This shift makes exploration a meta-level optimization problem, but useful supervision for exploration strategies is expensive and delayed because their quality often becomes apparent only after long discovery rollouts.

paragraphs.en: A broader line of work studies agents that improve their own components during interaction. Prior methods evolve model weights ( Huang et al., 2026c ; Huang et al., 2026a ; Li et al., 2026a ) , agent harnesses ( Lee et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ) , contexts ( Zhang et al., 2026d ) , skills ( Zhang et al., 2026a ; Ouyang et al., 2026a ; Wu et al., 2026b ) , model behavior through test-time learning ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Yuksekgonul et al., 2026 ; Yan et al., 2026a ; Wu et al., 2026a ) , rubrics ( Xiong et al., 2026 ) , environments ( Huang et al., 2026b ; Li et al., 2026c ; Li et al., 2026b ) and other applications ( Dai et al., 2026 ) . Most operate at the object level , improving components used for task execution or reasoning. Recent work has begun to optimize meta-level mechanisms, including search strategies and self-improvement procedures ( Liu et al., 2026a ; Yan et al., 2026a ; Wang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026c ; Kim et al., 2026 ) . However, such meta-level strategies are difficult to improve because their quality is often revealed only after costly long-horizon rollouts. Dream-RSI turns accumulated discovery history into replay simulators for off-policy evaluation and refinement of exploration policies, then redeploys the selected policy for new online discovery, closing a recursive self-improvement loop.

paragraphs.en: Prior work reuses agent experience as search history, context, memory, reusable skills, or training signals. DeltaEvolve structures evolutionary history through semantic deltas ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) ; SwarmResearch and MLEvolve use cross-branch or retrospective information to guide subsequent search ( Virk et al., 2026 ; Du et al., 2026 ) ; and other work improves how agents access and retain experience through evolving contexts, broader harness state, libraries, or skills ( Zhang et al., 2026d ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Ouyang et al., 2026a ) . We take a different view: rather than using exploration history only as context or memory for the next decision, we organize it as a replay simulator in which many alternative exploration controllers can be evaluated cheaply. This turns previously collected discovery experience into reusable feedback for meta-level optimization, alleviating the scarcity and high cost of training signals.

paragraphs.en: We presented Dream-RSI , a framework for the recursive self-improvement of exploration policies in long-horizon discovery. The central idea in Dream-RSI is to convert accumulated discovery history from static context into an active, replayable simulator, directly targeting the core bottleneck of meta-optimization: delayed and expensive feedback. By "dreaming" within replay simulators constructed from historical discovery trees, Dream-RSI evaluates candidate exploration policies rapidly and at negligible execution cost. Improved policies are then redeployed online, driving further discovery and expanding the simulator pool — closing the recursive self-improvement loop. Our experiments demonstrate competitive discovery quality across diverse domains and improved discovery-agent-call efficiency in several settings.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 Dream-RSI，一个用于长程探索中探索策略递归自我改进的框架。 Dream-RSI 的核心思想是将积累的探索历史从静态上下文转化为主动的、可重放的模拟器，直接针对元优化的核心瓶颈：反馈的延迟与高成本。 通过在由历史探索树构建的重放模拟器中“做梦”，Dream-RSI 能以极低的执行成本快速评估候选探索策略。 改进后的策略随后被重新部署到线上，驱动进一步的探索并扩充模拟器池——从而闭合递归自我改进的循环。 我们的实验表明，该方法在多个领域具有竞争力的探索质量，并在若干设置中提升了探索智能体调用的效率。

paragraphs.en: We present the detailed discovery process of PACEvolve ( Yan et al., 2026b ) on KernelBench in Figure 8 . For a controlled comparison, we allow PACEvolve a 48-hour wall-clock budget on each task and report its best-so-far performance throughout the search.

paragraphs.en: The following prompt is used to guide the discovery agent during online exploration. It requires the agent to inspect the complete available discovery history before proposing a new solution, explicitly reason about both successful and failed attempts, and avoid repeatedly exploiting a locally saturated direction.
paragraphs.zh: 以下提示词用于在在线探索过程中引导发现智能体。 它要求智能体在提出新方案之前先查看完整的可用发现历史，显式地对成功与失败的尝试都进行推理，并避免反复挖掘一个已经局部饱和的方向。

paragraphs.en: We provide the complete implementation of the Lasso-path solver discovered by Dream-RSI . As discussed in Section 4.3 , the solver combines strong-rule screening with adaptive Cauchy–Schwarz KKT pruning, disjoint active-set bookkeeping, lazy Gram-matrix construction, and hardware-aware optimizations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提供了由 Dream-RSI 发现的 Lasso 路径求解器的完整实现。 如第 4.3 节所述，该求解器结合了强规则筛选、自适应 Cauchy–Schwarz KKT 剪枝、不相交活动集记账、惰性 Gram 矩阵构建以及面向硬件的优化。
